title: nmea0183: Add ZDA sentence dissector
description:
Add sentence dissector for ZDA messages.
- It splits the time field into separated hour, minutes and seconds fields.
- The other fields are named and simply display their contents
- Report an expected but missing field
- Other sentence types are dissected by the existing code (split into unnamed fields)

### Tested
This pcap contains messages including ZDA sentences:
[nmea-simulator.pcapng](/uploads/db722637482f8a6786299330821e5a60/nmea-simulator.pcapng)

This pcap contains invalid variants of ZDA sentence:
[nmea-test-messages.pcapng](/uploads/ea46dd80d3d90b01b28d264c0a3925ab/nmea-test-messages.pcapng)

I have run 1000 iterations of `fuzz-test.sh` with these captures.

notes.body:
Hi @caspermeijn 

can you fix

```
packet-nmea0183.c:568 proto_tree_add_uint called for hf_nmea0183_checksum_calculated - item type is FT_UINT8 but call has len 2
packet-nmea0183.c:454:5: warning: Value stored to 'offset' is never read [deadcode.DeadStores]
```

The solution for the checksum warning is a bit ugly. The checksum refers to two bytes, but the bytes are the hex of a 8 bit value. So it doesn't exactly match. I chose to only highlight a single byte to suppress the warning.

Fixed the offset by not writing it, which breaks the code pattern, but that is fine.

Yes, it is very reasonable.  There are many ways to get from the full or partial contents of some bytes to a value that may or not fit within the obvious range of values. On balance, I am thinking that it would be less confusing if I remove the warning as it applies to calls to proto_tree_add_uint().  Some real issues have been spotted, but quite a few false positives as well.
OK, I will highlight the two bytes and add a comment to describe the situation. This means that the first warning will not be fixed.
